The graph of $y=f(t)$ is shown above. Which of the following could be $f(t),$ where $u$ denotes the unit step function?
feedback.worked_solution:
The unit step function $u(t)$ is defined as

$$
u(t)={\begin{aligned}1,\,t\ge 0, \\ 0,\,t<0.\end{aligned}
$$

The graph of $y=u(t)$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14037461/assets/9fb8c20672705e9d68e69d32e7ff3499ec71560e10aa85136b3f3ad75c5fb5ed.png)

Notice that to transform $y=u(t)$ to the given function $y=f(t),$ we perform the following transformations:

- First, we shift $y=u(t)$ by $1$ unit to the right, giving $y=u(t-1).$

- There is no vertical scaling or offset.

Therefore, we conclude that $f(t)=u(t-1).$
